sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Oh, there's a horse.
sentences.zh: 噢，那儿有匹马。

sentences.en: And this is friend of the show, Sean Cole.
sentences.zh: 这位是本节目的老朋友，肖恩·科尔。

sentences.en: I'm at West 39th and 11th in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 我现在在曼哈顿西39街和第11大道的交汇处。

sentences.en: And there's a horse.
sentences.zh: 那儿确实有匹马。

sentences.en: A horse-drawn carriage, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，是那种马拉的马车。

sentences.en: There aren't just random horses wandering around Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 曼哈顿街头可不会随随便便就有马在乱逛。

sentences.en: Though there probably were at some point.
sentences.zh: 虽然在某个时期可能确实有过。

sentences.en: I am actually going to meet a woman to talk about cows.
sentences.zh: 其实我正要去见一位女士，聊聊牛的事。

sentences.en: It's hard to believe now.
sentences.zh: 现在很难相信了。

sentences.en: Now, this area is really industrial.
sentences.zh: 现在这一带非常工业化。

sentences.en: There's a bus depot.
sentences.zh: 有个公交车调度站。

sentences.en: But this part of Manhattan, the westernmost part,
sentences.zh: 但曼哈顿的这一部分，也就是最西边，

sentences.en: between, say, 34th and 39th Streets,
sentences.zh: 大概在34街到39街之间，

sentences.en: this was cow country.
sentences.zh: 曾经是牛群出没的地方。

sentences.en: So, we're talking the late 19th, early 20th centuries.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是19世纪末到20世纪初。

sentences.en: You had cattle being herded across 12th Avenue,
sentences.zh: 当时牛群会被赶过第12大道，

sentences.en: which is now the West Side Highway.
sentences.zh: 也就是现在的西侧高速公路。

sentences.en: Nicola Twilley is the woman I wanted to talk to about cows.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉·特威利就是我想聊聊牛的那位女士。

sentences.en: She writes a blog called Edible Geography.
sentences.zh: 她写了一个叫《可食用地理》的博客。

sentences.en: There are pictures of 12th Avenue
sentences.zh: 有一些第12大道的照片，

sentences.en: showing the cattle here, showing cowboys, which is crazy.
sentences.zh: 上面有牛群，还有牛仔，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Get a long little doggie.
sentences.zh: 赶快走吧，小牛儿。

sentences.en: And cows were brought to this part of town to be made into beef.
sentences.zh: 牛被带到城里的这一带是为了加工成牛肉。

sentences.en: You've heard of the meat packing district?
sentences.zh: 听说过肉类加工区吗？

sentences.en: Well, this was like the meat hacking district.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这儿就像是“肉类切割区”。

sentences.en: It was nicknamed Abattoir Place,
sentences.zh: 它曾被称为“屠宰场广场”，

sentences.en: and it was a hive of bone boilers and hide stretchers and lard renderers.
sentences.zh: 是熬骨头、拉皮子和提炼猪油的聚集地。

sentences.en: So this, if you can picture it,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你能想象一下，

sentences.en: would have been a disassembly line for every single part of a cow.
sentences.zh: 这里曾是牛身上每一个部位的拆解流水线。

sentences.en: The cows would be ferried across the Hudson River from New Jersey
sentences.zh: 牛群会从新泽西州穿过哈德逊河，

sentences.en: on a cowboat
sentences.zh: 坐着运牛船，

sentences.en: and land at the dock here.
sentences.zh: 然后在码头登陆。

sentences.en: And at first, you know,
sentences.zh: 起初，你知道，

sentences.en: marching a few cows across 12th Avenue to the slaughterhouse was fine.
sentences.zh: 赶几头牛穿过第12大道去屠宰场还没什么问题。

sentences.en: You can hold up traffic for that.
sentences.zh: 为了这个你可以阻断交通。

sentences.en: But then came more cows.
sentences.zh: 但后来牛越来越多了。

sentences.en: And more cows.
sentences.zh: 牛更多了。

sentences.en: And more folks in their carriages.
sentences.zh: 坐马车的人也更多了。

sentences.en: And then the train came through.
sentences.zh: 接着火车也开过来了。

sentences.en: And cars.
sentences.zh: 还有汽车。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, cows are in the way.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，牛成了路障。

sentences.en: I mean, cows move at a different pace.
sentences.zh: 我是说，牛的行进速度是不一样的。

sentences.en: And so there were reports of epic cow jams on 12th Avenue.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有报道称第12大道发生了严重的“牛堵”。

sentences.en: What does a cow jam look like?
sentences.zh: “牛堵”是什么样子的？

sentences.en: That sounds horrible.
sentences.zh: 听起来太可怕了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I think it was just people felt like, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想当时人们只是觉得，你知道，

sentences.en: the pace of cows and cowboys and cow droving on 12th Avenue
sentences.zh: 第12大道上牛群、牛仔和赶牛的节奏

sentences.en: was no longer suited to modern life.
sentences.zh: 已经不再适应现代生活了。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: This is what we're here to talk about today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天来聊的话题。

sentences.en: I cannot wait.
sentences.zh: 我迫不及待了。

sentences.en: Me neither.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: Here we go.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: That's why people invented things like the cow tunnel.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们发明了像“牛隧道”这样的东西。

sentences.en: The cow tunnel.
sentences.zh: 牛隧道。

sentences.en: Cow tunnel.
sentences.zh: 牛隧道。

sentences.en: Oh, it's the beSt.
sentences.zh: 噢，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Let's hear it again.
sentences.zh: 让我们再听一遍。

sentences.en: Cow tunnel.
sentences.zh: 牛隧道。

sentences.en: Cattle tunnels.
sentences.zh: 牛群隧道。

sentences.en: Cow tunnels.
sentences.zh: 牛隧道。

sentences.en: Whenever you say it, it's funny.
sentences.zh: 无论什么时候说出来，都觉得好笑。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I mean, you have to love them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你不得不爱上它们。

sentences.en: Cow tunnels.
sentences.zh: 牛隧道。

sentences.en: Cow tunnels.
sentences.zh: 牛隧道。

sentences.en: In Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 在曼哈顿。

sentences.en: Or as Nicola called them in a piece she wrote for Gizmodo,
sentences.zh: 或者像尼古拉在为Gizmodo写的一篇文章中称呼它们的那样，

sentences.en: The Lost Cow Tunnels of New York City.
sentences.zh: 《纽约市失落的牛隧道》。

sentences.en: And when Nicola says that people invented things like the cow tunnel,
sentences.zh: 当尼古拉说人们发明了像牛隧道这样的东西时，

sentences.en: for the purposes of this story, that really could mean one of two things.
sentences.zh: 就这个故事而言，这实际上可能意味着两件事之一。

sentences.en: Either people invented the tunnels to march the cows underneath 12th Avenue to the abattoir,
sentences.zh: 要么是人们发明了隧道来把牛赶到第12大道地下的屠宰场，

sentences.en: or people invented this crazy cock and bull story about the cow tunnels.
sentences.zh: 要么是人们编造了这个关于牛隧道的荒唐故事。

sentences.en: More bull than cock in this case.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，编造的成分更多。

sentences.en: Because everybody loves a good, vaguely plausible urban myth.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都喜欢听那种听起来似是而非的都市传说。

sentences.en: And so, Nicola Twilley has been on a years-long quest to figure out whether the cow tunnels ever actually existed.
sentences.zh: 所以，尼古拉·特威利花了多年时间去探寻牛隧道是否真的存在。

sentences.en: Because, after all, the idea of cows loping along under your feet in New York City,
sentences.zh: 因为毕竟，牛在纽约市的地底下漫步的想法，

sentences.en: at least how we think of New York City now, is insane.
sentences.zh: 至少以我们现在对纽约市的印象来看，简直是疯了。

sentences.en: And this is a woman who writes a blog that's generally about food and place.
sentences.zh: 而她是一位专门写关于食物和地点的博客的作家。

sentences.en: And if anything exists at that same intersection, it is the cow tunnel.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么东西存在于那个交叉点上，那一定是牛隧道。

sentences.en: Just a dedicated infrastructure for animals like that.
sentences.zh: 就是那种专门为动物建造的基础设施。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's a new genre of architecture.
sentences.zh: 这是一种新的建筑流派。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The cow tunnel.
sentences.zh: 牛隧道。

sentences.en: When you think about all of the tubes and tunnels and weird things that are underneath the street,
sentences.zh: 当你想到街道下面所有的管道、隧道和奇怪的东西时，

sentences.en: we have tunnels for cars, we have tunnels for subways,
sentences.zh: 我们有汽车隧道，有地铁隧道，

sentences.en: we have all these tubes filled with electrical cables and the internet and all this,
sentences.zh: 我们有所有这些装满电缆、互联网线路等等的管道，

sentences.en: I mean, why shouldn't the cows have their own subterranean infrastructure, too?
sentences.zh: 我是说，为什么牛不能拥有它们自己的地下基础设施呢？

sentences.en: Nicola first happened on the cow tunnel story by chance.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉是偶然间发现了牛隧道的故事。

sentences.en: So I was reading a book called Raising Steaks by Betty Fussell.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在读贝蒂·福塞尔写的《饲养牛排》一书。

sentences.en: It's Fussell, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实是福塞尔（Fussell）。

sentences.en: Steaks, of course, is spelled S-T-E-A-K-S.
sentences.zh: 牛排（Steaks），当然，拼写是S-T-E-A-K-S。

sentences.en: Yes, the kind that could be porterhouse or, uh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，那种可以是丁骨牛排或者，呃，是的。

sentences.en: Or T-bone.
sentences.zh: 或者T骨牛排。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or sirloin.
sentences.zh: 或者西冷牛排。

sentences.en: Any of the above.
sentences.zh: 以上任何一种都可以。

sentences.en: Rump.
sentences.zh: 臀肉。

sentences.en: Strip loin.
sentences.zh: 腰脊肉。

sentences.en: Rump.
sentences.zh: 臀肉。

sentences.en: I like saying rump.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢说“臀肉”这个词。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Skirt.
sentences.zh: 裙边肉。

sentences.en: And she's reading along, and there was this one little passage on page 22.
sentences.zh: 她读着读着，在第22页有一小段话。

sentences.en: You could miss it quite easily if you were reading too faSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你读得太快，很容易就会错过它。

sentences.en: It's a sort of two-line thing.
sentences.zh: 那大概只有两行字。

sentences.en: And she says,
sentences.zh: 她说，

sentences.en: Traffic was so heavy in the 1870s that a cow tunnel, in quotation marks, was, and capitalized, actually,
sentences.zh: 19世纪70年代交通非常拥堵，以至于一条“牛隧道”（加了引号，而且实际上是大写的），

sentences.en: was built beneath 12th Avenue to serve as an underground passage.
sentences.zh: 被建在第12大道下方，用作地下通道。

sentences.en: And it's rumored to be there still, awaiting designation as a landmark site.
sentences.zh: 而且据传它至今仍在那里，等待被指定为地标遗址。

sentences.en: And then she just carries on, you know.
sentences.zh: 然后她就继续往下写了，你知道的。

sentences.en: As late as 1880, Horowitz writes, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 霍洛维茨写道，早在1880年，巴拉巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: That's one, that's literally one sentence.
sentences.zh: 那是一句，字面上就是一句话。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I thought, that's weird.
sentences.zh: 我想，这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: I wonder if they're still there.
sentences.zh: 不知道它们是不是还在那儿。

sentences.en: So I googled it.
sentences.zh: 所以我谷歌了一下。

sentences.en: And then what did you find?
sentences.zh: 然后你发现了什么？

sentences.en: I found Brian Whiprod, I think is how he pronounces his name.
sentences.zh: 我找到了布莱恩·惠普罗德，我想他是这么读他的名字的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's how I pronounce it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也是这么读的。

sentences.en: Brian Whiprod is a utility specialist for Weidlinger Associates in New York.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩·惠普罗德是纽约魏德林格联合公司的公用设施专家。

sentences.en: It's a structural engineering firm.
sentences.zh: 那是一家结构工程公司。

sentences.en: What I do for Weidlinger is figure out how to get from point A to point B underground in New York City.
sentences.zh: 我在魏德林格的工作就是弄清楚在纽约市地下如何从A点到达B点。

sentences.en: Like if Con Edison is cutting a trench for electrical cables, they need a navigator.
sentences.zh: 比如如果联合爱迪生公司要挖沟铺设电缆，他们就需要一个导航员。

sentences.en: As well as investigate all kinds of anomalies and strange things that they find underground when doing digs.
sentences.zh: 以及调查他们在挖掘时在地下发现的各种异常和奇怪的东西。

sentences.en: So Brian went searching for the truth about cow tunnels more than 10 years before Nicola.
sentences.zh: 所以布莱恩在尼古拉之前10多年就开始寻找牛隧道的真相了。

sentences.en: In 1997, he published an article in a local, local newspaper called the Tribeca Trib, which is what Nicola found in her web search.
sentences.zh: 1997年，他在一份名为《翠贝卡论坛报》的当地报纸上发表了一篇文章，这就是尼古拉在网络搜索中找到的内容。

sentences.en: The headline was Bum Steer.
sentences.zh: 标题是《糟糕的指引》。

sentences.en: I will summarize it here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里总结一下。

sentences.en: Brian's talking to a con ed worker named Fred.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩在和一位名叫弗雷德的联合爱迪生公司工人交谈。

sentences.en: Just Fred, huh?
sentences.zh: 就叫弗雷德？

sentences.en: Just Fred.
sentences.zh: 就叫弗雷德。

sentences.en: No last name.
sentences.zh: 没有姓。

sentences.en: And Fred says he was watching a work crew install a new drainage basin downtown.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德说他当时正在看施工队在市中心安装一个新的排水盆。

sentences.en: Which is, by the way, nowhere near the site of those old slaughterhouses.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，那地方离那些旧屠宰场遗址远着呢。

sentences.en: They dig and dig and then finally they hit this kind of wooden barrier.
sentences.zh: 他们挖啊挖，最后撞上了一种木质屏障。

sentences.en: Wooden.
sentences.zh: 木头的。

sentences.en: They break through it and it's hollow on the other side.
sentences.zh: 他们打破它，发现另一边是空的。

sentences.en: And then a quote unquote old man from the neighborhood steps up and says, I see you found the cow tunnel.
sentences.zh: 然后一位附近的老人走过来，说：“我看到你们找到牛隧道了。”

sentences.en: So Brian walks this story around, asks a whole mess of people.
sentences.zh: 所以布莱恩到处打听这个故事，问了很多人。

sentences.en: And everybody's heard of the cow tunnel.
sentences.zh: 每个人都听说过牛隧道。

sentences.en: But when they talk about it, the facts are never the same.
sentences.zh: 但当他们谈论它时，事实从来都不一样。

sentences.en: But A, it's somewhere different.
sentences.zh: 但首先，它总是在不同的地方。

sentences.en: And B, it's made of different iteMs.
sentences.zh: 还有B，它是由不同的材料制成的。

sentences.en: And C, it was built at a different time.
sentences.zh: 还有C，它是在不同的时间建造的。

sentences.en: And when Brian finally circles back to Fred, Fred says, well, actually, I never saw it.
sentences.zh: 当布莱恩终于回过头来问弗雷德时，弗雷德说，嗯，其实我从来没见过。

sentences.en: It was a buddy of mine who saw it.
sentences.zh: 是我一个朋友看到的。

sentences.en: So again, that's how Brian told the story in his article in 1997.
sentences.zh: 所以再说一次，这就是布莱恩在1997年的文章中讲述这个故事的方式。

sentences.en: Sitting in his office with me in 2014, he told it this way.
sentences.zh: 2014年，他坐在办公室里跟我讲的时候，却是这样说的。

sentences.en: We were digging some test pits for Verizon.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正在为威瑞森公司挖一些测试坑。

sentences.en: Wait, but so you were there and digging and...
sentences.zh: 等等，所以你当时在场，正在挖掘，然后……

sentences.en: Right, and so we've dug down about five feet and there's this brick curved surface that looks like a vaulted roof.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们挖了大约五英尺深，那里有一个砖砌的弧形表面，看起来像个拱形屋顶。

sentences.en: So now the story has completely changed in Brian's mind.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，布莱恩脑海中的故事已经完全变了。

sentences.en: Suddenly, he's the one watching the work crew, not Fred.
sentences.zh: 突然间，变成他在监视施工队，而不是弗雷德。

sentences.en: And in this telling, the blockage they hit while digging is brick, not wood.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个版本里，他们挖掘时撞到的障碍物是砖块，而不是木头。

sentences.en: And he talked this way for another 10 minutes before he finally stopped and said, wait a second.
sentences.zh: 他又这样讲了10分钟，才终于停下来，说，等等。

sentences.en: You know what, you sort of caught me in the beginning of this because I was like, gee, I could have sworn I saw it.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，你刚开始确实把我绕进去了，因为我当时想，天哪，我敢发誓我见过它。

sentences.en: And then you're just like, you know what, I'm thinking back at the article.
sentences.zh: 然后你就像是，你知道吗，我在回想那篇文章。

sentences.en: Well, I didn't.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我其实没见过。

sentences.en: And so I'm doing the same damn thing Fred did, aren't I?
sentences.zh: 所以我正在做和弗雷德一样该死的事情，不是吗？

sentences.en: Want me to tell you how big it is and where it goes?
sentences.zh: 想让我告诉你它有多大，通向哪里吗？

sentences.en: I see cattle tunnels every day, man.
sentences.zh: 伙计，我每天都能看到牛隧道。

sentences.en: There's one over there.
sentences.zh: 那边就有一个。

sentences.en: I know, I started doing the same damn thing.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我开始做同样该死的事情了。

sentences.en: This is what happens with the cow tunnels and why the truth of them is so hard to get a hold of.
sentences.zh: 这就是牛隧道发生的情况，也是为什么它们的真相如此难以捉摸的原因。

sentences.en: It's like as soon as you start to retell the story, it gets loose and begins to bend.
sentences.zh: 就像你一旦开始重述这个故事，它就会变得松散并开始扭曲。

sentences.en: It's like an instant fishtail, except it's about cows.
sentences.zh: 就像瞬间甩尾一样，只不过是关于牛的。

sentences.en: And somehow the folklore of it just stretches further and further out until nobody can remember how the story started.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，关于它的民间传说越传越远，直到没人记得故事是怎么开始的。

sentences.en: And so when Nicola Twilley wrote her first blog post about the cow tunnels in 2010, she went solely off of Brian's article, which uncovered nothing,
sentences.zh: 所以当尼古拉·特威利在2010年写下她关于牛隧道的第一篇博文时，她完全是基于布莱恩那篇什么都没揭露的文章，

sentences.en: and that one line in the Betty Fussell book.
